issues.title: ❌ Low Text Contrast
issues.description: Some text may be difficult to read for people with low vision. Text and background colors need a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1
how_to_fix: ✏️ Increase contrast between text and background
✏️ Use darker text on light backgrounds or lighter text on dark backgrounds
✏️ Test with a contrast checker tool to ensure 4.5:1 ratio for normal text
✏️ For large text (18pt+), maintain at least 3:1 contrast ratio

issues.title: ✅ Adequate Text Size
issues.description: Text appears to be appropriately sized for comfortable reading
how_to_fix: Great! Your text size appears readable for all users

issues.title: ✅ Good Color Independence
issues.description: Design doesn't appear to rely solely on color for conveying meaning
how_to_fix: Excellent! Your design includes non-color indicators for important information

issues.title: ✅ Adequate Touch Target Size
issues.description: Interactive elements appear to have adequate size for easy tapping
how_to_fix: Great! Your touch targets appear to be appropriately sized

issues.title: 📏 Keep Sentences Short
issues.description: Sentences should be 15-20 words maximum. Short sentences are easier to read and remember
how_to_fix: ✏️ Break long sentences into shorter ones
✏️ One idea per sentence is ideal
✏️ Aim for 15-20 words on average
✏️ Remove unnecessary phrases
✏️ BEFORE: 'The system, which has been designed with modern technologies, will help users to complete their tasks more effectively and efficiently'
✏️ AFTER: 'The system helps users work efficiently. It uses modern technologies.'

issues.title: 💬 Use Simple Words
issues.description: Use common, everyday words instead of complex jargon. This helps all users understand your content
issues.best_practice: Use everyday words that 6th grade students would understand
how_to_fix: ✏️ Replace complex words with simpler alternatives
✏️ Use 'use' instead of 'utilize'
✏️ Use 'help' instead of 'facilitate'
✏️ Use 'start' instead of 'commence'
✏️ Use 'end' instead of 'terminate'
✏️ Use 'change' instead of 'modification'
✏️ BEFORE: 'We will facilitate the implementation of comprehensive modifications'
✏️ AFTER: 'We will help make important changes'

issues.title: 📄 Break Up Text
issues.description: Use headings, short paragraphs, and bullet points. Long blocks of text are intimidating and hard to scan
issues.best_practice: Use headings, short paragraphs (3-4 sentences), and lists
how_to_fix: ✏️ Use clear headings and subheadings
✏️ Keep paragraphs to 3-4 sentences
✏️ Use bullet points for lists
✏️ Add white space between sections
✏️ Use short lines (50-75 characters per line)
✏️ Use bold to highlight important terms
✏️ Avoid large blocks of solid text

issues.title: 🎯 Use Active Voice
issues.description: Active voice is clearer and more direct. It shows who is doing the action
issues.best_practice: Subject performs action (active) rather than action performed on subject (passive)
how_to_fix: ✏️ Use active voice: Subject + Verb + Object
✏️ PASSIVE (hard): 'The button was clicked by the user'
✏️ ACTIVE (clear): 'The user clicked the button'
✏️ PASSIVE (hard): 'The mistake was made by the team'
✏️ ACTIVE (clear): 'The team made the mistake'
✏️ PASSIVE (hard): 'It was decided that...'
✏️ ACTIVE (clear): 'We decided that...'
✏️ Avoid words like: 'was', 'been', 'were', 'by the'

summary.focus: Apply these readability best practices to your text content

issues.title: 🔥 Visual Attention Areas
how_to_fix: ✏️ Your design naturally draws attention to: Middle-Right, Middle-Center, Top-Right
✏️ Make sure these hot spots contain important content
✏️ If not important, reduce contrast in these areas
✏️ Use high-attention areas for calls-to-action (CTAs)
✏️ Important content should be in prominent positions
✏️ Consider user attention span - focus on 1-2 key messages
✏️ Secondary information should be in lower-attention areas
